course: Autonomous Aerial Systems: Control, Planning & SLAM
intro: This course provides a comprehensive and structured introduction to the field of Aerial Robotics, designed for students looking to build a strong technical foundation in autonomous aerial systems. Grounded in both theory and practical application, it covers the full pipeline from flight mechanics to intelligent autonomy.

weeks.content: An introduction to quadrotor flight, MATLAB basics & 1D control systems. Students familiar with PID controllers, explore system dynamics through simulations & tackle motor selection and thrust-to-weight ratio analysis.

A deep dive into quadrotor kinematics and dynamics — covering Euler angles, rotation matrices, the 12-state state vector, equations of motion & the Newton-Euler formulation. Students simulate quadrotor agility and stopping distance using MATLAB.

Development of 2D and 3D linear controllers for the quadrotor. Topics include nested feedback loops, trajectory tracking, hover control, PD/PID controller design & MATLAB-based simulation of full 3D quadrotor control.
Introduction to autonomous navigation — covering Pose Graph SLAM, loop closure, path planning algorithms (A* and RRT) & an overview of swarm robotics and multi-agent coordination.

weeks.week: By the end of the course
weeks.content: Students will have built a solid foundation in quadrotor dynamics, control theory & autonomous navigation, backed by practical MATLAB simulations and assignments — qualifying them for the hands-on hardware implementation phase.

evaluation: Attendance in Speaker sessions (A%), Weekly Assignments (B%), Capstone Project (C%). Passing Criteria: 75% attendance in sessions and weekly assignments

intro: Kickstart your data science journey with our beginner-friendly "Data Science Fundamentals with Python" course! Start from core Python skills, explore data handling and data visualization with exciting libraries transitioning to ML through supervised and unsupervised learning algorithms with in-depth yet carefully curated easy-to-follow resources finishing off with a perfect real world project to reinforce key concepts while building your portfolio. This isn’t just a course; it’s your gateway to mastering the transformation of Basic raw data into Brilliant actionable intelligence!

weeks.content: Python Basics, Jupyter Notebooks, Numpy, Pandas, Matplotlib, Seaborn, and Worksheet 1.

Supervised Learning - Regression: Domains of Analytics, Scikit-Learn Essentials, Linear Regression, Multiple Linear Regression, Time Series Analysis, Time Series Forecasting, Anomaly detection, and Worksheet 2.

Supervised Learning - Classification: Regression vs Classification, Logistic Regression, Decision Trees & Random Forests, Optional Classification algorithms (SVM, KNN), Neural Networks, Probability distributions and Central Limit Theorem, and Worksheet 3.

Unsupervised Learning: Intro to Unsupervised Learning, K-Means Clustering, Hierarchical Clustering, Gaussian Mixture Models, Dimensionality Reduction (PCA, SVD, LDA), Matrix Factorization, and Capstone Project.

evaluation: There will be 3 worksheets and 1 final capstone project. 1st Phase worksheet, Atleast one among the 2nd and 3rd Phase worksheets and Capstone project are necessary for certification

intro: Dive into the world of data analysis using the most accessible tools out there. Whether you're a beginner or just looking to brush up your skills, this course takes you through Excel and SQL with bite-sized videos, practical assignments, designed to fit into your daily routine.

weeks.content: Excel: Introduction to spreadsheets, Basics of spreadsheets, Columns, row and cell formatting, Basics of formulas, Introduction to functions, Absolute and Relative referencing, Introduction to data quality & importing file data, Data cleaning techniques.
Excel: Sorting & Filtering, Some important functions, VLOOKUP & HLOOKUP functions, Pivot Tables. SQL: Installation and setup, Introduction, Queries in SQL, Functions in SQL, Operators in SQL.
Excel: All about Charts, Dashboarding. SQL: All about clauses, SQL Joins, Subquery in SQL.

intro: Ever wondered what happens inside a chemical reaction — at the level of atoms and electrons — before it shows up in your test tube? Computational chemistry lets you simulate molecules on a computer, predict how they behave, and even discover new materials and drugs without lifting a pipette.

weeks.content: Energy, Geometry, and students First Simulation: Potential Energy Surface (PES), coordinates (bond length, angle, dihedral), local and global minima, optimization algorithms conceptually (steepest descent, conjugate gradient), and hands-on WebMO activities.

Molecular Mechanics: Treating Atoms Like Balls and Springs — Hooke's law, angular springs, torsion periodic functions, Lennard-Jones/Coulomb potentials, force fields (AMBER, CHARMM, OPLS, UFF), parameterization, and butane torsional energy curve exercises.

Molecular Dynamics: Making Atoms Move — velocities, Newton's F = ma, Verlet integration algorithm, timesteps, ensembles (NVE, NVT, NPT), temperature and pressure control, and running liquid water simulations in LAMMPS.

The Quantum Leap: Why Electrons Matter + DFT Intuition — Schrödinger equation, Born–Oppenheimer approximation, Density Functional Theory (DFT) basics, functionals (LDA, GGA, hybrid), and a guided DFT calculation on small molecules.

Pick a small molecule of your choice (3–10 heavy atoms) and carry out a multi-method comparative study. Understand limitations, methods (MM vs MD vs QM), read research papers, and present compiled findings.

evaluation: A=20 B=40 C=40 passing criteria will be 60% overall score

intro: Consulting 101 is a beginner-friendly, structured course designed to introduce students to the fundamentals of consulting. It focuses on developing structured thinking, business frameworks, and case-solving skills through practical concepts like guesstimates, market entry, profitability, and growth strategy, mirroring real consulting problem-solving.

weeks.content: Week 1 – Introduction to consulting and core problem-solving tools, including structured thinking (MECE, issue trees) and guesstimates to develop logical and analytical approaches.
Week 2 – Market and industry analysis using frameworks like market entry, Porter’s Five Forces, PESTEL, SWOT, and market sizing (TAM/SAM/SOM) to understand businesses and competitive landscapes.
Week 3 – Application of consulting frameworks to real business problems, covering profitability analysis, value chains, growth strategies (4Ps, 3Cs, Ansoff), and pricing concepts.

weeks.week: By the end of the course

intro: Product Management 101 is a 4-week beginner-to-intermediate course designed for students who want to explore PM as a career or build the foundational thinking that makes great product builders. No prior experience needed, just curiosity and a bias for problem-solving.

weeks.content: Week 1 — An introduction to the PM role, how products are built from 0 to 1, and how to think about users through research, personas, the Jobs-to-be-Done framework, and empathy mapping.

Week 2 — A deep dive into the PM craft: conducting user interviews, running competitive analysis, writing PRDs, building roadmaps, prioritizing ruthlessly using frameworks like RICE, KANO, and MoSCoW, and aligning stakeholders with OKRs.

Week 3 — The metrics and experimentation layer, how PMs measure success using frameworks like AARRR and HEART, analyze funnels and retention, run A/B tests, and structure product design answers for interviews end-to-end.

Week 4 — Interview preparation and applied PM thinking, product improvement cases, app critiques, root cause analysis, GTM and pricing strategy, Fermi estimation, and behavioral questions using the STAR framework.

weeks.week: By the end of the course
weeks.content: You'll be able to identify user problems, size opportunities, write a PRD, build a roadmap, define success metrics, and walk into a PM interview with a structured, confident approach to any product design or analytical question thrown at you.

evaluation: Attendance in Speaker sessions (33.3%) Weekly Assignments (33.3%) Capstone Project (33.3%). Certification: Successful completion of assignments and capstone criteria.

course: Simulation and Optimisation of Smart Energy Systems
intro: A practical and technology-oriented introduction to modern energy systems with emphasis on renewable energy integration, computational simulation, optimisation techniques, smart grid technologies, IoT-enabled energy monitoring, and AI-based intelligent energy management systems.

weeks.content: Week 1 — Fundamentals of Modern Energy Systems. Students will be introduced to the evolution of conventional and smart energy systems, including the integration of renewable energy technologies such as solar and wind power. The week also covers energy demand patterns, load profiles, grid challenges, and the need for simulation and optimisation in modern energy infrastructure.

Week 2 — Simulation and Computational Modelling. This week focuses on computational modelling and simulation techniques used in energy systems. Students will learn the basics of Python and Google Colab, model solar and battery systems, understand battery State of Charge (SOC), and analyse energy datasets using Pandas and Matplotlib for visualisation and interpretation of simulation results.

Week 3 — Optimisation of Energy Systems. Students will explore optimisation techniques used in energy management and sustainable power systems. Topics include optimisation fundamentals, objective functions, constraints, energy scheduling, peak demand reduction, battery management, and linear programming using tools such as SciPy Optimise and PuLP. A hands-on activity on battery scheduling optimisation will also be included.

Week 4 — Smart Energy Technologies and Future Systems. The final week introduces emerging technologies transforming the energy sector, including smart grids, IoT-enabled monitoring systems, EV charging infrastructure, intelligent energy management, AI applications in energy systems, digital twins, and data-driven analytics for future sustainable energy solutions.

weeks.week: By the End of the Course
weeks.content: Students will gain foundational knowledge of modern energy systems, renewable energy integration, and smart grid technologies. They will develop hands-on skills in Python-based simulation, energy data analysis, and optimisation techniques, while also exploring emerging technologies such as IoT, EV infrastructure, and AI-driven energy systems.

evaluation: Grading Format - 4 quizzes, each with 25% weightage. Passing Criteria: Minimum 50% overall score across all quizzes. Participants must attempt at least 3 out of 4 weekly quizzes to complete the course.

intro: The course bridges engineering and markets through logical optimization puzzles. Over four weeks, you will dissect counterintuitive paradoxes. From how free solar power crashes electricity prices to why energy efficiency can increase fuel consumption.

weeks.content: Week 1 — Macro Energy Dynamics and Resource Horizons. Students will explore the economics of finite energy resources and consumer behaviour in energy markets. Topics include resource depletion strategies, Hotelling’s Rule, the Green Paradox, energy efficiency gaps, and Jevon’s Paradox, providing insight into how energy markets and human behaviour shape long-term energy consumption.

Week 2 — Power Grid Operations and Market Regulations. This week focuses on electricity market structures and grid economics. Students will learn how grid auctions determine electricity prices, how transmission networks operate under physical constraints, and how concepts such as merit order curves, uniform price auctions, locational marginal pricing, and regulatory monopolies influence modern power systems.

Week 3 — Clean Energy Economics and the Solar Paradox. Students will analyse the economic and operational challenges introduced by renewable energy integration. The course covers net load profiles, the duck curve, renewable energy subsidies, renewable cannibalisation, and the missing money problem, helping students understand the complexities of maintaining stable and profitable clean energy markets.

Week 4 — Grid Flexibility, Storage, and Decarbonisation Policy. The final week explores energy storage economics, battery arbitrage, grid flexibility, and long-term decarbonisation strategies. Students will study how future grid assets generate value through revenue stacking, manage capital risk, and support reliable low-carbon energy systems.

weeks.week: By the End of the Course
weeks.content: Students will gain a strong understanding of energy market economics, power grid operations, renewable energy integration, and energy storage systems. They will develop the ability to analyse electricity markets, understand policy and pricing mechanisms, and evaluate the economic forces driving the global clean energy transition.

evaluation: Weekly quizzes 4× 25%. Evaluation criteria: 1) Attempted atleast 3 quizzes 2) more than 40% in quizzes

intro: Master the art of launching and scaling a startup in just three weeks. Learn from industry experts about idea generation, growth strategies, and building a winning team to achieve entrepreneurial success.

weeks.content: Week 1: Startup foundation and Understanding Product-Market Fit. The first week focuses on the essential building blocks of a startup. You'll learn how to transform a compelling idea into a robust product, assemble an exceptional team, and execute flawlessly. Key topics include problem-solving with passion, the importance of execution, strategic pivoting, evaluating long-term value, and future planning. Through case studies of companies like Airbnb, Tesla, and Netflix, you'll gain a deep understanding of how these principles apply in the real world.

Week 2: Growth Strategies and Marketing techniques. In the second week, the course shifts to various growth strategies crucial for a startup’s success. You'll explore SEO, email marketing, SMS, and push notifications, with an emphasis on deliverability and user engagement. Learn how to create products users love and the importance of exceptional customer support. Highlights include keyword research, link building, triggered marketing campaigns, and leveraging word-of-mouth for organic growth.

Week 3: Building Culture and Strategic Management. The final week focuses on building a strong company culture and effective team management. Insights from leaders like Ben Silberman and the Collison brothers will guide you in hiring individuals who align with your company’s values. Topics include transparency, onboarding, managing people and resources, and making strategic decisions. You'll also learn the significance of location, contrarian thinking, and intelligent risk-taking in the startup landscape.
Finalization and pitch evaluation processing.

weeks.week: By the end of the course

course: AI in Entrepreneurship - Innovate, Launch, Scale
intro: This 4-week course introduces students to the intersection of entrepreneurship and artificial intelligence. You’ll learn how to ideate, validate, build, and scale a startup using practical AI tools. Each week focuses on a new stage of the entrepreneurial journey-from understanding the startup lifecycle and market research to building MVPs with no-code AI platforms and preparing AI-powered pitch decks.

weeks.content: Week 1: Introduction to Entrepreneurship & Foundations of AI — Understanding the entrepreneurial mindset and the startup lifecycle; Overview of AI and machine learning (no technical background needed); Applications of AI in real-world businesses; AI in the startup landscape: opportunities and examples; Hands-on: Explore ChatGPT, Notion AI, and other beginner-friendly tools.

Week 2: AI for Market Research & Opportunity Identification — Using AI tools for market research and trend analysis; Customer persona creation and segmentation with AI assistance; Competitive landscape mapping using AI scrapers and research assistants; Tools: Browse AI, ChatGPT, Perplexity AI, Similarweb.

Week 3: Building MVPs and Prototypes with AI & No-Code Tools — Understanding MVPs and product-market fit; Introduction to no-code tools (Bubble, Glide, Canva, Figma, Tally); Integrating AI APIs or models into your startup idea; Case studies: Jasper AI, Copy.ai, Looka, Synthesia.

Week 4: Scaling, Pitching & Ethical AI Use — Using AI in sales, marketing, and customer support automation; Creating AI-powered pitch decks and fundraising strategies; Tools: Beautiful.ai, ChatGPT for scripting, Decktopus, SlidesAI; Discussion: Responsible use of AI, ethics, bias, and data privacy.

weeks.week: By the end of the course
weeks.content: Participants will have developed a complete AI-powered startup concept along with practical exposure to AI tools used for ideation, market research, prototyping and preparing AI-powered pitch decks.

prerequisites: No coding experience required; Basic familiarity with startups, business ideas, or willingness to explore new tools; Curiosity to learn and experiment with AI-driven platforms
evaluation: Assignments and project mapping. Minimum 60% overall score. Certification: Attend all speaker sessions (1 session weekly, Total 4 sessions); Submission of all weekly assignments and final project

intro: An introduction to the fundamentals of finance, covering personal finance, asset classes, fundamental analysis, and technical analysis, designed to equip students with practical tools for informed financial decision-making.

weeks.content: Week 1 Personal Finance: Practical frameworks for budgeting, saving, and building long-term financial security, equipping students with essential tools to manage their finances and make informed decisions early in their careers.

Week 2 Asset Classes: An introduction to key asset classes including equity, debt, real estate, and commodities, with a focus on their role in portfolio diversification, income generation, and risk management.

Week 3 Fundamental Analysis: Evaluating companies through financial statements and key ratios, helping students assess stocks and determine intrinsic value using the principles of fundamental analysis.

Week 4 Technical Analysis: Understanding price trends, chart patterns, and market indicators to analyse stock movements and develop data-driven trading and investment perspectives. The bootcamp culminates in a capstone project where students apply everything they have learned across the four weeks to a real-world financial scenario.

evaluation: Weekly Assignments + Capstone Project execution. Certification: Students must meet the minimum attendance requirement (3 out of 4 sessions), submit at least 3 out of 4 weekly assignments, and complete the capstone project to receive a certificate of completion.

course: Introduction to Machine Learning and AI
intro: This course provides a beginner-friendly introduction to Machine Learning, Deep Learning, and modern AI systems. Participants will learn the foundations of ML workflows, neural networks, transformers, and Large Language Models through a combination of theory, hands-on coding, and mini projects.

weeks.content: Week 1 - Introduction to Machine Learning: Overview of ML and AI; Supervised vs Unsupervised Learning; Loss Functions and Gradient Descent; ML lifecycle; Learning prerequisites: Python, NumPy, Pandas, Matplotlib, Jupyter Notebook, and Google Colab; Data preprocessing techniques; Train/Validation/Test splits; Basic text cleaning; Tokenization concepts and Byte Pair Encoding (BPE).

Week 2 - Classical ML and Deep Learning Foundations: Classical NLP techniques: Bag-of-Words and TF-IDF; Logistic Regression for sentiment analysis; Limitations of classical ML methods; Evaluation metrics: accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, confusion matrix, and loss; Introduction to Deep Learning; Neurons, Perceptrons, and Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLPs); Hidden layers and activation functions (ReLU, tanh); Softmax and classification outputs; Embeddings and vector representations; One-hot encoding limitations; Word2Vec and semantic embeddings.

Week 3 - Transformers and Modern AI Systems: Introduction to Transformers and their applications; Overview of the Transformer architecture; Encoder vs Decoder models (BERT vs GPT-style models); Working with HuggingFace APIs and pipelines; Sentiment analysis, translation, and chatbot pipelines; Prompt engineering techniques; Few-shot prompting and Chain-of-Thought prompting; Introduction to RLHF and supervised fine-tuning concepts; Introduction to Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and vector databases.

Week 4 - Building AI Applications: Building an AI-powered assistant application; Prompting and customizing cloud-hosted LLMs; Introduction to RAG-based assistants; Creating interfaces using Streamlit or Gradio; Deploying and demonstrating AI applications; Overview of advanced AI topics like (Reinforcement Learning, Stable Diffusion, DPO/PPO, Agentic AI, SSMs).

weeks.week: By the end of the course
weeks.content: Participants will be able to understand the fundamentals of ML and AI, work with Python ML libraries, and deploy applications.

prerequisites: No prior Machine Learning experience required. Basic programming familiarity is helpful but not mandatory.
evaluation: Weekly Assignments (40%) Capstone Project (60%). Certification: Submission of at least 2 weekly assignments, Successful completion and submission of the capstone project

intro: The Quantum Circuits course breaks down the heart of quantum computers, shows how computation happens, and teaches you to build a decomposition algorithm which turns a matrix into a circuit of logic gates. This is extremely important today because every quantum computer from Google's to IBM's has a limited set of gates to work with, and this algorithm addresses that.

weeks.content: Week 1 - Intro to quantum computing, qubits, and circuits.
Week 2 - Mathematics of a universal gate set & circuit synthesis.
Week 3 - Implementing a quantum circuit compiler.
Week 4 - Using the compiler to simulate Grover’s Algorithm. Test how many qubits a laptop can simulate.

weeks.week: By the end of the course
weeks.content: You will have learnt the nitty-gritties of how quantum computers compute, worked with the intricate math behind quantum logic gates, and written an algorithm to decompose a circuit into logic gates.

prerequisites: Some experience in coding in Python is welcome, but not required.
evaluation: Week 1-3: Assignments (50% = 10% + 10% + 30%), Week 4: Project (50%). Certification: Passing criteria: 40%. Subject to change depending on student performance.

intro: Ever wondered why people make the choices they do, in negotiations, competitions, or even everyday decisions? Game Theory gives you the mathematical tools to actually understand and predict strategic behaviour. Over this course, you will learn what it even means to be "rational", and build your way up through some of the most elegant ideas in economics and mathematics.

weeks.content: Week 1: Why game theory, the game of chess, introduction to normal form games (Prisoner's Dilemma), Idea of Rationality
Week 2: Model of Normal form games, Concept of domination, WDSE, SDSE, Nash equilibrium, PSNE,
Week 3: Concept of Mixed Strategy, Idea of MSNE, Existence and Computation of MSNEs, Bayesian games/games with imperfect info
Week 4: Extensive form games, behavioral strategies and kuhn's theorem, stochastic extensive form games

evaluation: B=100. Certification: Passing Criteria=60%

intro: Several processes in nature are out of equilibrium, as such, they can not be modeled within the framework of regular thermodynamics/statistical physics. This course seeks to introduce the learner to interesting out of equilibrium phenomenon like brownian motion and diffusion by looking for the statistical laws that govern them.

weeks.content: Week 1 : Basics of probability and classical statistical mechanics (Kolmogorovs axioms, PDFs, moments, cumulants, conditional probability, probability in classical stat mech, microcanonical and canonical ensemble, statistical mechanics from the feynman lectures)

Week 2 : The Chapmann Kolmogorov equation, Master equation for jump processes, Diffusion and Birth-Death processes as examples, Transition rates from the hamiltonian, detailed balance, continuum limit of the master equation
Week 3 : Langevin dynamics, gaussian white noise, OU process, fluctuation - dissipation relation, relation to Fokker-Planck equations
Week 4 : Basic simulations (Kinetic Monte Carlo for the master equation and additive noise for Langevin)

evaluation: B=100. Certification: Passing Criteria=TBD

intro: This course is a beginner-friendly introduction to full stack web development, designed to help students build modern web applications from scratch. Participants will learn the fundamentals of programming, frontend and backend development, databases, deployment, and software engineering practices through hands-on learning and practical assignments.

weeks.content: Week 1 - Programming & Development Foundations: Introduction to web development and software workflows; Basics of programming using Python and JavaScript; Variables, loops, conditionals, functions, and problem-solving; Coding fundamentals and logic building; Introduction to Git and GitHub for version control and collaboration; Basic command line usage and development setup.

Week 2 - Frontend Development & UI Design: Structure of websites using HTML; Styling using CSS; Responsive web design principles; Introduction to JavaScript for frontend interactivity; UI/UX fundamentals and creating visually appealing interfaces; Building interactive and user-friendly frontend pages.

Week 3 - Backend Development: Introduction to backend systems and APIs; Server-side development fundamentals; Handling routes, requests, and responses; Connecting frontend and backend; Authentication basics and user management; Building dynamic web applications.

intro: Every business runs on data, but most of it is locked inside websites, messy spreadsheets, and scattered systems. The people who can pull it out, clean it up, store it properly, and turn it into a dashboard are the ones companies actually pay for. This bootcamp will make you go from your first line of Python to shipping a complete data pipeline.

weeks.content: Week 1: Web Scraping & Data Retrieval Methods — Learn where data actually comes from. Understand how websites and APIs work, write your first Python scripts to pull real data from the web. By the end of the week you'll have scraped your own dataset that you'll keep building on for the rest of the bootcamp.

Week 2: Excel Fundamentals — Everyone thinks they know Excel. Almost no one actually does. The difference between dragging cells around for hours and finishing the same work in ten minutes comes down to a handful of formulas most people have never touched.

Week 3: SQL & Querying Data — Excel breaks at a million rows. SQL doesn't. Learn the single most valuable skill in data work: querying databases. Filter, group, join, and aggregate data to answer real business questions, using SQLite.

Week 4: PostgreSQL & Power BI Dashboarding — Graduate from a learning database to a production one. Set up PostgreSQL, load your data properly, then connect it to Power BI to build interactive dashboards with filters, KPIs, and visuals stakeholders can actually use.

evaluation: Assignments + Capstone mapping. Certification: Passing Criteria 2 or 3 assignments and 1 capstone project

intro: Every company is racing to automate with AI and the people who can build it are the most in-demand. In 4 weeks you will go from your first LLM API call to shipping a fully autonomous multi-agent workflow. The same architecture powering the most advanced AI products in production today.

weeks.content: Week 1: Understanding LLMs: Prompting & APIs — Learn how LLMs work, why prompt structure matters, and how to move from chatting in a browser to controlling a model through.
Week 2: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) & Fine Tunning — Teach your LLM to answer from your own documents using RAG, and learn when fine-tuning makes more sense.

Week 3: Agentic AI (MCPs, LangChain, LangGraph) — Go from generating text to taking action. Build an agent that can use tools, make decisions, and execute multi-step tasks using LangChain, LangGraph, and MCP.

Week 4: Multi Agent Workflows and Capstone Project — Learn how to design autonomous systems where multiple specialised agents collaborate under an orchestration layer that routes tasks, manages state, and handles failures.

evaluation: Compulsory Assignments + Project metrics. Certification: 2 out of 3 assignments and 1 capstone project are compulsory for certification
